sw.B: Sikilizeni neno hili, enyi nyumba ya Israeli, maombolezo haya ninayoyaimba juu yenu:

decisions.choice: a lament: a funeral song sung over the dead
decisions.reason: The word qinah is used for the song that mourners sang over someone who had died, as David did over Saul and Jonathan (2 Samuel 1:17). Amos sings it over Israel while the nation is still alive and prosperous, as if it were already dead. The short poem that follows (verse 2) has the uneven rhythm of such songs, a longer line followed by a shorter one, as in Lamentations.

decisions.choice: I: the prophet speaks, and the Lord GOD's words follow in verse 3
decisions.reason: The speaker takes up the lament himself, and in verse 3 he passes on what the Lord GOD says. As elsewhere in the book, the prophet's words and the LORD's run together without a break, and neither takes quotation marks.

decisions.choice: raise (B); funeral song ... singing (R); People of Israel (R)
decisions.reason: To 'lift up' a lament is to begin singing it aloud, so Balanced says 'raise'. Readable says 'funeral song', so that readers know what kind of song it is (m1), and 'people of Israel' for 'house of Israel', since 'house' here means the whole family of Israel's descendants.

decisions.choice: "lamento" (L, B); "canto fúnebre" (R)
decisions.reason: Qinah is the song sung over the dead; R names it, as the English R does.

decisions.choice: "complainte" (L, B); "chant de deuil" (R) for the lament (qinah)
decisions.reason: The term sheet's wording for the funeral song in the prophets.

source.text: נָֽפְלָה֙ לֹֽא־תוֹסִ֣יף ק֔וּם בְּתוּלַ֖ת יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל נִטְּשָׁ֥ה עַל־אַדְמָתָ֖הּ אֵ֥ין מְקִימָֽהּ׃

records.literal_gloss: She has fallen, she will not again rise, [the] virgin of Israel; she has been forsaken on her land, there [is] none raising her up.

en.L: Fallen, she will not rise again, the virgin Israel; \q forsaken on her land, there [is] no one to raise her up.
en.B: Fallen, never to rise again, is Virgin Israel; \q she lies abandoned on her own land, with no one to lift her up.
en.R: Israel, like a young woman, has fallen, \q and she will never get up again. \q She lies deserted on her own land, with no one to help her up.

es.L: Ha caído, no volverá a levantarse la virgen Israel; \q abandonada está sobre su tierra, no [hay] quien la levante.
es.B: Ha caído para no levantarse más la virgen Israel; \q yace abandonada en su propia tierra, sin nadie que la levante.
es.R: Israel, como una muchacha, ha caído, \q y nunca más volverá a levantarse. \q Yace abandonada en su propia tierra, sin nadie que la ayude a levantarse.

fr.L: Elle est tombée, elle ne se relèvera plus, la vierge d’Israël ; \q elle est abandonnée sur sa terre, il n’y a personne pour la relever.
fr.B: Elle est tombée pour ne plus se relever, la vierge Israël ; \q elle gît abandonnée sur sa propre terre, et personne ne la relève.
fr.R: Israël, comme une jeune fille, est tombée, \q et elle ne se relèvera jamais. \q Elle gît abandonnée sur sa propre terre, et personne ne l’aide à se relever.

sw.L: Ameanguka, hatainuka tena, bikira Israeli; \q ameachwa juu ya nchi yake, hakuna [mtu] wa kumwinua.
sw.B: Ameanguka, hatainuka tena kamwe, Bikira Israeli; \q amelala ameachwa katika nchi yake mwenyewe, bila mtu wa kumwinua.
sw.R: Israeli, aliye kama msichana mdogo, ameanguka, \q wala hatainuka tena kamwe. \q Amelala ameachwa peke yake katika nchi yake, bila mtu wa kumsaidia kuinuka.

decisions.choice: the virgin Israel: the nation pictured as a young woman not yet married
decisions.reason: The phrase pictures the whole people as a young woman. In a funeral song it adds to the grief: she has died young, before her life was full. Jeremiah uses the same picture (Jeremiah 31:4, 21).

decisions.choice: she has fallen ... she has been forsaken: spoken as already done
decisions.reason: The verbs are past tense. Israel was still standing and prosperous when Amos spoke, but the lament speaks of its fall as already certain, as if the funeral had begun.

decisions.choice: Virgin Israel (B, as Jeremiah 31:4); Israel, like a young woman (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced writes 'Virgin Israel' as a name, as Jeremiah 31:4 does. Readable keeps the picture of a young woman but makes Israel the subject, since 'virgin' as a title for a nation is unfamiliar.

decisions.choice: "la virgen Israel" (L, B)
decisions.reason: As Jeremiah 31:4 in Spanish; Spanish keeps a lowercase "virgen", since the English capital in "Virgin Israel" (B) marks a title Spanish does not capitalize.

decisions.choice: "la vierge d'Israël" (L), "la vierge Israël" (B), "Israël, comme une jeune fille" (R), with feminine agreement
decisions.reason: The forms of the published French Jeremiah 31:4 and 31:21 at Literal and Balanced; the past tense "est tombée" keeps the Hebrew's lament over what is spoken of as already done.

decisions.choice: "bikira Israeli" (L); "Bikira Israeli" (B); "Israeli, aliye kama msichana mdogo" (R)
decisions.reason: As the daughter titles in the term sheet ("bikira binti Yuda", "Bikira Binti Yuda"): lowercase at Literal, a capitalised title at Balanced, and plain words at Readable.

source.text: כִּ֣י כֹ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה הָעִ֛יר הַיֹּצֵ֥את אֶ֖לֶף תַּשְׁאִ֣יר מֵאָ֑ה וְהַיּוֹצֵ֥את מֵאָ֛ה תַּשְׁאִ֥יר עֲשָׂרָ֖ה לְבֵ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃ס

records.literal_gloss: For thus says [the] Lord Yahweh: the city that goes out a thousand will have left a hundred, and that goes out a hundred will have left ten, for [the] house of Israel.

en.L: For thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}: \q The city that goes out a thousand [strong] will have a hundred left, \q and [the one] that goes out a hundred [strong] will have ten left, to the house of Israel.
en.B: For the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says this: \q The city that marches out a thousand strong will be left with a hundred, \q and the one that marches out a hundred strong will be left with ten, in the house of Israel.
en.R: This is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says: \q When a city of Israel sends out a thousand soldiers, only a hundred will survive. \q When a town sends out a hundred, only ten will be left.

es.L: Porque así dice el Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}}: \q La ciudad que sale con mil se quedará con cien, \q y la que sale con cien se quedará con diez, para la casa de Israel.
es.B: Porque el Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}} dice esto: \q La ciudad que sale a la guerra con mil hombres se quedará con cien, \q y la que sale con cien se quedará con diez, en la casa de Israel.
es.R: Esto es lo que dice el Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}}: \q Cuando una ciudad de Israel envíe mil soldados, solo sobrevivirán cien. \q Cuando un pueblo envíe cien, solo quedarán diez.

fr.L: Car ainsi parle le Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}} : \q La ville qui sortait [forte de] mille n’en aura plus que cent, \q et [celle] qui sortait [forte de] cent n’en aura plus que dix, pour la maison d’Israël.
fr.B: Car le Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}} dit ceci : \q La ville qui partait en guerre avec mille hommes n’en gardera que cent, \q et celle qui partait avec cent n’en gardera que dix, dans la maison d’Israël.
fr.R: Voici ce que dit le Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}} : \q Quand une ville d’Israël enverra mille soldats, il n’en survivra que cent. \q Quand un village en enverra cent, il n’en restera que dix.

sw.L: Kwa maana Bwana {{divine_name:MUNGU|Yahwe}} asema hivi: \q Mji unaotoka [na watu] elfu utabakiwa na mia, \q na [ule] unaotoka [na watu] mia utabakiwa na kumi, kwa nyumba ya Israeli.
sw.B: Kwa maana hivi ndivyo Bwana {{divine_name:MUNGU|Yahwe}} asemavyo: \q Mji unaotoka kwenda vitani na watu elfu utabaki na mia moja, \q na ule unaotoka na watu mia moja utabaki na kumi, katika nyumba ya Israeli.
sw.R: Hili ndilo Bwana {{divine_name:MUNGU|Yahwe}} analosema: \q Mji wa Israeli ukipeleka askari elfu vitani, ni mia moja tu watakaonusurika. \q Mji ukipeleka askari mia moja, ni kumi tu watakaobaki.

decisions.choice: goes out a thousand: sends out a thousand men to war
decisions.reason: A city 'went out' when its fighting men marched out to battle, and a town's troops were counted in units of a thousand and a hundred (1 Samuel 8:12; 2 Samuel 18:1). Nine out of ten will be lost. The remnant left is too small to be a comfort.

decisions.choice: to the house of Israel: this is what Israel will have left
alternatives: a note on the whole saying: 'so it will be for the house of Israel'
decisions.reason: The phrase stands at the end of the verse and says whose army this is. It may belong to the last clause ('ten left to the house of Israel') or to the whole saying ('so it will be for the house of Israel'). The sense is the same.

decisions.choice: Thus says the Lord GOD (L); The Lord GOD says this (B); This is what the Lord GOD says (R)
decisions.reason: The formula koh 'amar keeps the wording settled for Isaiah and Jeremiah at each level, with 'the Lord GOD' for Adonai with the divine name.

decisions.choice: of Israel; soldiers; survive (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says 'soldiers' and 'survive' to make plain that the city's fighting men are meant and that only a tenth of them will live (m1). It moves 'Israel' into the first sentence, where the reader needs it.

source.text: כִּ֣י כֹ֥ה אָמַ֛ר יְהוָ֖ה לְבֵ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל דִּרְשׁ֖וּנִי וִֽחְיֽוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: For thus says Yahweh to [the] house of Israel: seek me and live.

en.L: For thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} to the house of Israel: \q Seek {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and live!
en.B: For {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says this to the house of Israel: \q Seek {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and live!
en.R: This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says to the people of Israel: \q Seek {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and you will live.

es.L: Porque así dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} a la casa de Israel: \q ¡{{plural_you:Búsquenme|Buscadme}} y {{plural_you:vivirán|viviréis}}!
es.B: Porque {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} dice esto a la casa de Israel: \q ¡{{plural_you:Búsquenme|Buscadme}} y {{plural_you:vivirán|viviréis}}!
es.R: Esto es lo que dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} al pueblo de Israel: \q {{plural_you:Búsquenme|Buscadme}} y {{plural_you:vivirán|viviréis}}.

fr.L: Car ainsi parle {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} à la maison d’Israël : \q Cherchez-{{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, et vivez !
fr.B: Car {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} dit ceci à la maison d’Israël : \q Cherchez-{{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, et vous vivrez !
fr.R: Voici ce que dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} au peuple d’Israël : \q Cherchez-{{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, et vous vivrez.

sw.L: Kwa maana {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} asema hivi kwa nyumba ya Israeli: \q Nitafuteni, mkaishi!
sw.B: Kwa maana hivi ndivyo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} asemavyo kwa nyumba ya Israeli: \q Nitafuteni, mpate kuishi!
sw.R: Hili ndilo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} analowaambia watu wa Israeli: \q Nitafuteni, nanyi mtaishi.

decisions.choice: seek me: turn to the LORD himself, to worship and obey him
decisions.reason: To 'seek' the LORD was to go to him in worship and prayer, to ask his will and follow it. Verse 5 sets this against going to the shrines: seeking the LORD is not the same as visiting his holy places. Verses 14-15 say what it means in practice: seek good, hate evil, and set up justice in the courts.

decisions.choice: and live: a promise as well as a command
decisions.reason: Two commands joined by 'and' in Hebrew often mean 'do this, and then this will follow'. Life here is the nation's survival, set against the funeral song of verses 1-2.

decisions.choice: "Búsquenme / Buscadme" written with the pronoun joined to the verb
decisions.reason: The object pronoun of God is joined to the imperative, so there is no free pronoun to carry a deity_pronoun span; the plural_you span carries both forms. "Y vivirán" says the promise in the command, as the meaning decision reads it.

source.text: וְאַֽל־תִּדְרְשׁוּ֙ בֵּֽית־אֵ֔ל וְהַגִּלְגָּל֙ לֹ֣א תָבֹ֔אוּ וּבְאֵ֥ר שֶׁ֖בַע לֹ֣א תַעֲבֹ֑רוּ כִּ֤י הַגִּלְגָּל֙ גָּלֹ֣ה יִגְלֶ֔ה וּבֵֽית־אֵ֖ל יִהְיֶ֥ה לְאָֽוֶן׃

records.literal_gloss: And do not seek Bethel, and [to] Gilgal do not go, and [to] Beersheba do not cross over; for Gilgal will surely go into exile, and Bethel will become nothing.

en.L: But do not seek Bethel, \q and do not go to Gilgal, \q and do not cross over to Beersheba; \q for Gilgal will certainly go into exile, \q and Bethel will become nothing.
en.B: Do not seek Bethel; \q do not go to Gilgal \q or cross over to Beersheba. \q For Gilgal is sure to go into exile, \q and Bethel will be reduced to nothing.
en.R: Do not go to Bethel to worship. \q Do not go to Gilgal, \q or cross the border to Beersheba. \q The people of Gilgal will be taken away as captives, \q and Bethel will become nothing.

es.L: Pero no {{plural_you:busquen|busquéis}} a Betel, \q ni {{plural_you:vayan|vayáis}} a Gilgal, \q ni {{plural_you:pasen|paséis}} a Beerseba; \q porque Gilgal ciertamente irá al destierro, \q y Betel se convertirá en nada.
es.B: No {{plural_you:busquen|busquéis}} a Betel; \q no {{plural_you:vayan|vayáis}} a Gilgal \q ni {{plural_you:crucen|crucéis}} hasta Beerseba. \q Porque Gilgal sin duda irá al destierro, \q y Betel quedará reducida a nada.
es.R: No {{plural_you:vayan|vayáis}} a adorar a Betel. \q No {{plural_you:vayan|vayáis}} a Gilgal, \q ni {{plural_you:crucen|crucéis}} la frontera para ir a Beerseba. \q La gente de Gilgal será llevada prisionera, \q y Betel quedará en nada.

fr.L: Mais ne cherchez pas Béthel, \q et n’allez pas à Guilgal, \q et ne passez pas à Beer-Shéba ; \q car Guilgal ira sûrement en exil, \q et Béthel deviendra néant.
fr.B: Ne cherchez pas Béthel ; \q n’allez pas à Guilgal \q et ne passez pas à Beer-Shéba. \q Car Guilgal partira en exil, c’est certain, \q et Béthel sera réduite à néant.
fr.R: N’allez pas à Béthel pour adorer. \q N’allez pas à Guilgal, \q et ne passez pas la frontière pour aller à Beer-Shéba. \q Les gens de Guilgal seront emmenés en captivité, \q et Béthel ne sera plus rien.

sw.L: Lakini msiitafute Betheli, \q wala msiende Gilgali, \q wala msivuke kwenda Beer-sheba; \q kwa maana hakika Gilgali itakwenda uhamishoni, \q na Betheli itakuwa si kitu.
sw.B: Msiitafute Betheli; \q msiende Gilgali \q wala msivuke kwenda Beer-sheba. \q Kwa maana hakika Gilgali itakwenda uhamishoni, \q na Betheli itageuka kuwa bure.
sw.R: Msiende Betheli kuabudu. \q Msiende Gilgali, \q wala msivuke mpaka kwenda Beer-sheba. \q Watu wa Gilgali watachukuliwa mateka, \q na Betheli itakuwa si kitu.

decisions.choice: Bethel, Gilgal, Beersheba: the great shrines where Israel worshiped
decisions.reason: Bethel was the royal shrine of the northern kingdom (7:13; 1 Kings 12:29-33), and Gilgal was another famous holy place (4:4; Hosea 4:15). Beersheba lay far to the south in Judah, so people from the north had to 'cross over' the border to go there on pilgrimage (8:14). All three were linked with the stories of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, or with Israel's entry into the land.

decisions.choice: a play on the names: Gilgal will go into exile, and Bethel ('house of God') will become nothing
decisions.reason: In Hebrew, 'Gilgal will surely go into exile' repeats the sounds of the name: haggilgal galoh yigleh. Bethel means 'house of God', and Amos says it will become 'aven, 'nothing' or 'trouble'. Hosea plays on the same word when he calls the town Beth-aven, 'house of nothing' (Hosea 4:15). The puns cannot be carried into translation, so a note gives them.

decisions.choice: go to Bethel to worship; cross the border; the people of Gilgal ... as captives (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says why people went to these towns, and that going to Beersheba meant crossing into Judah (m1). It says that the people of Gilgal will be taken away, since a town 'goes into exile' when its people are deported.

decisions.choice: the wordplay on Gilgal and Bethel is not kept
decisions.reason: The Hebrew plays on the sound of Gilgal (galoh yigleh, "go into exile") and on Bethel, "house of God", becoming nothing; Spanish cannot keep the sound, and the meaning footnote explains it.

source.text: דִּרְשׁ֥וּ אֶת־יְהוָ֖ה וִֽחְי֑וּ פֶּן־יִצְלַ֤ח כָּאֵשׁ֙ בֵּ֣ית יוֹסֵ֔ף וְאָכְלָ֥ה וְאֵין־מְכַבֶּ֖ה לְבֵֽית־אֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: Seek Yahweh and live, lest he rush like fire [on] the house of Joseph, and it devour, and there [is] none quenching [it] for Bethel.

en.L: Seek {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and live, \q lest {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} break out like fire [against] the house of Joseph, \q and it devour, with no one to quench [it] for Bethel.
en.B: Seek {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and live, \q or {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will sweep through the house of Joseph like fire; \q it will burn, and there will be no one at Bethel to put it out.
en.R: Seek {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and you will live. \q If you do not, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will rush on Israel like a fire. \q It will burn everything, and no one at Bethel will be able to put it out.

es.L: {{plural_you:Busquen|Buscad}} {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} y {{plural_you:vivirán|viviréis}}, \q no sea que irrumpa como fuego [contra] la casa de José, \q y la devore, sin que haya quien [lo] apague en Betel.
es.B: {{plural_you:Busquen|Buscad}} {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} y {{plural_you:vivirán|viviréis}}, \q o {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} caerá como fuego sobre la casa de José; \q la consumirá, y no habrá nadie en Betel que lo apague.
es.R: {{plural_you:Busquen|Buscad}} {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} y {{plural_you:vivirán|viviréis}}. \q Si no lo {{plural_you:hacen|hacéis}}, {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} caerá sobre Israel como un fuego. \q Lo quemará todo, y nadie en Betel podrá apagarlo.

fr.L: Cherchez {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, et vivez, \q de peur qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} ne fonde comme un feu [sur] la maison de Joseph, \q et qu’il ne dévore, sans personne pour [l’]éteindre pour Béthel.
fr.B: Cherchez {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, et vous vivrez ; \q sinon, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} fondra sur la maison de Joseph comme un feu ; \q il dévorera, et il n’y aura personne à Béthel pour l’éteindre.
fr.R: Cherchez {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, et vous vivrez. \q Sinon, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} se jettera sur Israël comme un feu. \q Ce feu brûlera tout, et personne à Béthel ne pourra l’éteindre.

sw.L: Mtafuteni {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} mkaishi, \q {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} asije akaivamia nyumba ya Yusufu kama moto, \q nao ukateketeza, bila mtu wa kuuzima kwa ajili ya Betheli.
sw.B: Mtafuteni {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} mpate kuishi, \q la sivyo {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} ataipitia nyumba ya Yusufu kama moto; \q utawaka, wala hapatakuwa na mtu huko Betheli wa kuuzima.
sw.R: Mtafuteni {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, nanyi mtaishi. \q Msipofanya hivyo, atawavamia Israeli kama moto. \q Utateketeza kila kitu, wala hakuna mtu huko Betheli atakayeweza kuuzima.

decisions.choice: the house of Joseph: the northern kingdom
decisions.reason: Joseph was the father of Ephraim and Manasseh, the largest tribes of the north, so 'the house of Joseph' stands for the northern kingdom of Israel (also 5:15; 6:6).

decisions.choice: for Bethel: the fire will reach Bethel, and the shrine can do nothing to stop it
decisions.reason: The fire will burn at Bethel and no one there will put it out. The shrine the people trusted cannot protect them; the fire may even begin there (compare 3:14).

decisions.choice: If you do not; Israel (R)
decisions.reason: Readable spells out 'lest' as 'If you do not', and says 'Israel' for 'the house of Joseph', since the name stands for the northern kingdom (m1).

source.text: הַהֹפְכִ֥ים לְלַעֲנָ֖ה מִשְׁפָּ֑ט וּצְדָקָ֖ה לָאָ֥רֶץ הִנִּֽיחוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: [O you] who turn into wormwood justice, and righteousness to [the] earth they cast down.

en.L: [You] who turn justice into wormwood, \q and cast righteousness down to the earth!
en.B: You turn justice into bitter wormwood \q and throw righteousness to the ground.
en.R: You turn justice into something bitter. \q You throw what is right to the ground.

es.L: ¡{{plural_you:Ustedes|Vosotros}}, los que {{plural_you:convierten|convertís}} en ajenjo el derecho, \q y {{plural_you:echan|echáis}} por tierra la justicia!
es.B: {{plural_you:Ustedes convierten|Vosotros convertís}} el derecho en amargo ajenjo \q y {{plural_you:echan|echáis}} por tierra la justicia.
es.R: {{plural_you:Ustedes convierten|Vosotros convertís}} la justicia en algo amargo. \q {{plural_you:Echan|Echáis}} por tierra lo que es correcto.

fr.L: [Vous] qui changez le droit en absinthe, \q et jetez à terre la justice !
fr.B: Vous changez le droit en absinthe amère \q et vous jetez la justice à terre.
fr.R: Vous changez la justice en quelque chose d’amer. \q Vous jetez par terre ce qui est juste.

sw.L: [Ninyi] mnaogeuza hukumu kuwa pakanga, \q na kuitupa haki chini!
sw.B: Mnaigeuza haki kuwa pakanga chungu \q na kuutupa uadilifu chini.
sw.R: Mnaigeuza haki kuwa kitu kichungu. \q Mnautupa uadilifu chini.

decisions.choice: those who turn: a new address, naming the people Amos accuses
alternatives: read as 'Woe to those who turn', as 5:18 and 6:1 begin
decisions.reason: The verse opens with 'the ones who turn', without a main verb, and then changes to 'they' in the second line. It reads like the start of a 'woe' saying such as 5:18 and 6:1, and it may be that the word 'woe' was once said or written before it. The Hebrew as it stands still names those who are accused, and the sense is the same either way.

decisions.choice: justice and righteousness: fair judgment in the courts and right dealing with others
decisions.reason: Mishpat is justice as it is done, above all in the courts at the city gate (verses 10, 12, 15). Tsedaqah is what is right: keeping faith with others, the poor above all. The pair runs through the book (5:24; 6:12). Here those Amos accuses turn justice into something bitter and throw what is right on the ground.

decisions.choice: wormwood: a bitter plant, a picture of what is bitter and harmful
decisions.reason: Wormwood is a plant with a very bitter taste (Deuteronomy 29:17; Jeremiah 9:14). Justice should be sweet and healing to those who are wronged; these judges make it bitter. 6:12 repeats the picture.

decisions.choice: bitter wormwood (B); something bitter; what is right (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced adds 'bitter' so that the point of the plant is clear. Readable says 'what is right' for tsedaqah, as the terms note settles for Amos, and 'something bitter' for wormwood, a plant few readers know (m3).

decisions.choice: "el derecho" / "la justicia" (L, B); "la justicia" / "lo que es correcto" (R)
decisions.reason: Mishpat and tsedaqah as the terms note sets for these books (Jeremiah 23:5), with the R wording of the English "justice / what is right".

decisions.choice: "le droit" and "la justice" (L, B); "la justice" and "ce qui est juste" (R), for mishpat and tsedaqah in the whole book
decisions.reason: The term sheet's pair for the Twelve, as Isaiah; Readable keeps the two ideas with common words.

decisions.choice: "hukumu" / "haki" (L); "haki" / "uadilifu" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Mishpat and tsedaqah in Amos, as Isaiah 28:17 and the term sheet; the same pair returns in 5:24 and 6:12.

source.text: עֹשֵׂ֨ה כִימָ֜ה וּכְסִ֗יל וְהֹפֵ֤ךְ לַבֹּ֨קֶר֙ צַלְמָ֔וֶת וְי֖וֹם לַ֣יְלָה הֶחְשִׁ֑יךְ הַקּוֹרֵ֣א לְמֵֽי־הַיָּ֗ם וַֽיִּשְׁפְּכֵ֛ם עַל־פְּנֵ֥י הָאָ֖רֶץ יְהוָ֥ה שְׁמֽוֹ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Making Pleiades and Orion, and turning to the morning deep darkness, and day [into] night he darkens; the one calling for the waters of the sea and he pours them out on [the] face of the earth, Yahweh [is] his name.

en.L: [He] who made [the] Pleiades and Orion, and turns deep darkness into morning, \q and darkens day into night, \q who calls the waters of the sea and pours them out on the face of the earth, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [is] {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name.
en.B: He made the Pleiades and Orion; he turns deep darkness into morning \q and darkens day into night. \q He calls up the waters of the sea and pours them out across the face of the earth: {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} made the stars, the Pleiades and Orion. He turns the darkest night into morning \q and makes the day as dark as night. \q He calls for the water of the sea and pours it out on the land. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name.

es.L: [Él] que hizo las Pléyades y Orión, y convierte en mañana las densas tinieblas, \q y oscurece el día como la noche, \q el que llama a las aguas del mar y las derrama sobre la faz de la tierra, {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} [es] {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} nombre.
es.B: Él hizo las Pléyades y Orión; {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} convierte en mañana las densas tinieblas \q y oscurece el día hasta hacerlo noche. \q Él llama a las aguas del mar y las derrama sobre la faz de la tierra: {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} es {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} nombre.
es.R: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} hizo las estrellas, las Pléyades y Orión. Él convierte en mañana la noche más oscura \q y hace que el día sea oscuro como la noche. \q Llama a las aguas del mar y las derrama sobre la tierra. {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} es {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} nombre.

fr.L: [Lui] qui a fait les Pléiades et Orion, et change en matin l’ombre de la mort, \q et obscurcit le jour en nuit, \q qui appelle les eaux de la mer et les répand sur la face de la terre, {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} [est] {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} nom.
fr.B: Il a fait les Pléiades et Orion ; {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} change en matin les ténèbres les plus profondes \q et obscurcit le jour pour en faire la nuit. \q Il appelle les eaux de la mer et les répand sur la face de la terre : {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} est {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} nom.
fr.R: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a fait les étoiles, les Pléiades et Orion. Il change en matin la nuit la plus noire \q et rend le jour aussi sombre que la nuit. \q Il appelle l’eau de la mer et la verse sur la terre. {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} est {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} nom.

sw.L: [Yeye] aliyeifanya Kilimia na Orioni, na kuligeuza giza nene kuwa asubuhi, \q na kuufanya mchana kuwa giza la usiku, \q ayaitaye maji ya bahari na kuyamwaga juu ya uso wa nchi, {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} [ndilo] jina {{deity_pronoun:lake|Lake}}.
sw.B: Yeye aliifanya Kilimia na Orioni; huligeuza giza nene kuwa asubuhi \q na kuufanya mchana kuwa giza kama usiku. \q Huyaita maji ya bahari na kuyamwaga juu ya uso wa nchi: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ndilo jina {{deity_pronoun:lake|Lake}}.
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliumba nyota, Kilimia na Orioni. Huligeuza giza kuu la usiku kuwa asubuhi \q na kuufanya mchana kuwa na giza kama usiku. \q Huyaita maji ya bahari na kuyamwaga juu ya nchi. {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ndilo jina {{deity_pronoun:lake|Lake}}.

decisions.choice: a hymn to the LORD as Creator, set inside the accusation
decisions.reason: Verses 8-9 break into the charge of verses 7 and 10 with lines of praise in the style of a hymn, like 4:13 and 9:5-6, each ending with 'the LORD is his name'. The God whom the unjust judges ignore is the one who rules the stars, day and night, and the sea. The hymn makes the threat more fearful, not less.

decisions.choice: Pleiades and Orion: two well-known groups of stars
decisions.reason: Kimah and Kesil are named together in Job 9:9 and 38:31 too. The usual identification is the star cluster of the Pleiades and the constellation Orion. The LORD who placed them in the sky is the God Israel has to answer to.

decisions.choice: deep darkness: the darkest dark
decisions.reason: Tsalmavet means very deep darkness (Psalm 23:4; Job 10:21). It was long read as 'shadow of death', from the sound of its parts, but it is one word for thick darkness.

decisions.choice: who calls for the waters of the sea: the same line returns in 9:6
decisions.reason: The line is repeated word for word in 9:6. It may picture the rain drawn up from the sea and poured on the land, or the flood (Genesis 7). Either way the LORD rules the waters.

decisions.choice: The LORD made the stars; the darkest night (R)
decisions.reason: Readable names the LORD at the start, since the hymn otherwise begins without a subject, and says 'the stars' so that readers know what the Pleiades and Orion are (m2).

decisions.choice: "l'ombre de la mort" (L)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the traditional rendering of the compound word, as the French Literal of Isaiah 9:1 does; Balanced and Readable say its sense.

decisions.choice: "Kilimia" for the Pleiades; "Orioni" for Orion
decisions.reason: "Kilimia" is the traditional Swahili name of the Pleiades, the cluster whose rising marks the farming year on the coast; Orion has no settled Swahili name in common use, so the international name is kept.

source.text: הַמַּבְלִ֥יג שֹׁ֖ד עַל־עָ֑ז וְשֹׁ֖ד עַל־מִבְצָ֥ר יָבֽוֹא׃

records.literal_gloss: The one who makes flash devastation on [the] strong, and devastation on [the] fortress comes.

en.L: who makes destruction flash out against the strong, \q so that destruction comes upon the fortress.
en.B: He makes destruction blaze out against the strong, \q and ruin comes upon the fortress.
en.R: He suddenly destroys those who are strong, \q and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} brings ruin on their fortresses.

es.L: el que hace brillar la destrucción sobre el fuerte, \q y la destrucción viene sobre la fortaleza.
es.B: Él hace estallar la destrucción contra el fuerte, \q y la ruina cae sobre la fortaleza.
es.R: Él destruye de repente a los que son fuertes, \q y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} hace caer la ruina sobre sus fortalezas.

fr.L: lui qui fait jaillir la destruction sur le fort, \q et la destruction vient sur la forteresse.
fr.B: Il fait éclater la destruction sur le puissant, \q et la ruine s’abat sur la forteresse.
fr.R: Il détruit soudain ceux qui sont forts, \q et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} fait tomber la ruine sur leurs forteresses.

sw.L: ambaye huufanya uharibifu umulike juu ya wenye nguvu, \q hata uharibifu ukaijia ngome.
sw.B: Huufanya uharibifu uwake ghafla juu ya wenye nguvu, \q na maangamizi yanaijia ngome.
sw.R: Huwaangamiza ghafla wale walio na nguvu, \q {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} huleta maangamizi juu ya ngome zao.

decisions.choice: makes flash: brings suddenly, like a flash of light
alternatives: makes destruction rise against the strong
decisions.reason: The verb is rare. In Job 9:27 and 10:20 and Psalm 39:14 it means to brighten up or to smile; here it seems to mean making destruction break out suddenly, like a flash. The sense of the line is plain even though the picture is uncertain: no strength or fortress can stand against him.

decisions.choice: suddenly destroys those who are strong (R)
decisions.reason: Readable gives the sense of the picture (m1) in plain words: the destruction comes suddenly.

source.text: שָׂנְא֥וּ בַשַּׁ֖עַר מוֹכִ֑יחַ וְדֹבֵ֥ר תָּמִ֖ים יְתָעֵֽבוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: They hate in the gate one who reproves, and one who speaks with integrity they abhor.

en.L: They hate the one who reproves in the gate, \q and they abhor the one who speaks with integrity.
en.B: They hate anyone who rebukes wrongdoing in court \q and detest whoever speaks honestly.
en.R: They hate anyone who speaks up against wrong in court. \q They hate anyone who tells the truth.

es.L: Aborrecen al que reprende en la puerta, \q y detestan al que habla con integridad.
es.B: Odian a quien denuncia la maldad en el tribunal \q y detestan a quien habla con honradez.
es.R: Odian a cualquiera que hable contra el mal en el tribunal. \q Odian a cualquiera que diga la verdad.

fr.L: Ils haïssent celui qui reprend à la porte, \q et ils ont en horreur celui qui parle avec intégrité.
fr.B: Ils haïssent quiconque dénonce le mal au tribunal \q et détestent celui qui parle honnêtement.
fr.R: Ils détestent quiconque s’oppose au mal au tribunal. \q Ils détestent quiconque dit la vérité.

sw.L: Wanamchukia yeye akemeaye langoni, \q na wanamchukia kabisa yeye asemaye kwa unyoofu.
sw.B: Wanamchukia kila anayekemea uovu mahakamani \q na kumchukia sana yeyote asemaye kweli.
sw.R: Wanamchukia mtu yeyote anayepinga uovu mahakamani. \q Wanamchukia mtu yeyote anayesema ukweli.

decisions.choice: in the gate: in the court held at the city gate
decisions.reason: The elders of a town sat in the open space by the city gate to hear cases and give judgment (Deuteronomy 21:19; Ruth 4:1-11). 'In the gate' therefore means 'in court' (verses 12 and 15).

decisions.choice: the one who reproves ... the one who speaks with integrity: a witness or judge who exposes wrong and tells the truth
decisions.reason: The first word is used of someone who argues a case or rebukes a wrongdoer; the second of someone who speaks honestly, without crookedness. These are the people a fair court needs, and the powerful hate them.

decisions.choice: in court; rebukes wrongdoing (B); speaks up against wrong (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say 'in court', since many readers do not know what the city gate was used for (m1), and say what the one who 'reproves' does.

decisions.choice: "en el tribunal" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The court that sat at the city gate is named as a court at B and R, as the English does; L keeps "en la puerta".

source.text: לָ֠כֵן יַ֣עַן בּוֹשַׁסְכֶ֞ם עַל־דָּ֗ל וּמַשְׂאַת־בַּר֙ תִּקְח֣וּ מִמֶּ֔נּוּ בָּתֵּ֥י גָזִ֛ית בְּנִיתֶ֖ם וְלֹא־תֵ֣שְׁבוּ בָ֑ם כַּרְמֵי־חֶ֣מֶד נְטַעְתֶּ֔ם וְלֹ֥א תִשְׁתּ֖וּ אֶת־יֵינָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Therefore, because you trample on [the] poor and a levy of grain you take from him, houses of hewn stone you have built, but you will not live in them; vineyards of delight you have planted, but you will not drink their wine.

en.L: Therefore, because you trample on the poor and take a levy of grain from {{gender:them|him}}, \q you have built houses of hewn stone, but you will not live in them; \q you have planted pleasant vineyards, \q but you will not drink their wine.
en.B: Therefore, because you trample on the poor and force them to hand over their grain, \q you have built houses of cut stone, but you will not live in them; \q you have planted fine vineyards, \q but you will not drink their wine.
en.R: You crush poor people and force them to give you their grain. \q So you will never live in the fine stone houses you have built. \q You will never drink wine from the beautiful vineyards you have planted.

es.L: Por tanto, ya que {{plural_you:pisotean|pisoteáis}} al pobre y le {{plural_you:exigen|exigís}} tributo de grano, \q {{plural_you:edificaron|edificasteis}} casas de piedra labrada, pero no {{plural_you:habitarán|habitaréis}} en ellas; \q {{plural_you:plantaron|plantasteis}} viñas hermosas, \q pero no {{plural_you:beberán|beberéis}} su vino.
es.B: Por tanto, ya que {{plural_you:pisotean|pisoteáis}} al pobre y lo {{plural_you:obligan|obligáis}} a entregar su grano, \q {{plural_you:han construido|habéis construido}} casas de piedra labrada, pero no {{plural_you:vivirán|viviréis}} en ellas; \q {{plural_you:han plantado|habéis plantado}} viñas hermosas, \q pero no {{plural_you:beberán|beberéis}} su vino.
es.R: {{plural_you:Aplastan|Aplastáis}} a los pobres y los {{plural_you:obligan|obligáis}} a dar{{plural_you:les|os}} su grano. \q Por eso nunca {{plural_you:vivirán|viviréis}} en las hermosas casas de piedra que {{plural_you:han construido|habéis construido}}. \q Nunca {{plural_you:beberán|beberéis}} el vino de las hermosas viñas que {{plural_you:han plantado|habéis plantado}}.

fr.L: C’est pourquoi, parce que vous piétinez le pauvre et que vous prenez de lui un impôt de grain, \q vous avez bâti des maisons en pierre de taille, mais vous n’y habiterez pas ; \q vous avez planté des vignes délicieuses, \q mais vous n’en boirez pas le vin.
fr.B: C’est pourquoi, parce que vous écrasez le pauvre et le forcez à vous livrer son grain, \q vous avez bâti des maisons en pierre de taille, mais vous n’y habiterez pas ; \q vous avez planté de belles vignes, \q mais vous n’en boirez pas le vin.
fr.R: Vous écrasez les pauvres et vous les forcez à vous donner leur grain. \q Alors vous n’habiterez jamais les belles maisons de pierre que vous avez bâties. \q Vous ne boirez jamais le vin des belles vignes que vous avez plantées.

sw.L: Kwa hiyo, kwa sababu mnamkanyaga maskini na kumtoza ushuru wa nafaka, \q mmejenga nyumba za mawe yaliyochongwa, lakini hamtakaa ndani yake; \q mmepanda mashamba mazuri ya mizabibu, \q lakini hamtakunywa divai yake.
sw.B: Kwa hiyo, kwa sababu mnawakanyaga maskini na kuwalazimisha kuwapa nafaka zao, \q mmejenga nyumba za mawe yaliyochongwa, lakini hamtakaa ndani yake; \q mmepanda mashamba mazuri ya mizabibu, \q lakini hamtakunywa divai yake.
sw.R: Mnawaponda maskini na kuwalazimisha kuwapa nafaka zao. \q Kwa hiyo hamtaishi kamwe katika nyumba nzuri za mawe mlizojenga. \q Hamtakunywa kamwe divai kutoka mashamba mazuri ya mizabibu mliyopanda.

decisions.choice: you trample: you crush, or tax, the poor
alternatives: you levy a tax on the poor
decisions.reason: The verb occurs only here. It has usually been taken as a form of a verb meaning to trample. A word in Akkadian, the language of Assyria and Babylon, means to collect a tax, and that sense fits the parallel line, 'you take a levy of grain'. Either way the rich are living off the poor.

decisions.choice: a levy of grain: a share of the harvest taken from poor farmers
decisions.reason: Mas'at is a portion or payment that is carried off. Here the rich take part of the grain of poor farmers, perhaps as rent for land or as payment on a debt.

decisions.choice: houses you will not live in, vineyards whose wine you will not drink: the curse of the covenant
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy 28:30, 39 warns that if Israel breaks the covenant, people will build houses and not live in them, and plant vineyards and not drink their wine; Zephaniah 1:13 repeats it. Houses of hewn, squared stone were a luxury (1 Kings 7:9). In 9:14 the curse is turned round: the restored people will drink the wine of their own vineyards.

decisions.choice: them (gender setting, L); force them to hand over (B, R)
decisions.reason: 'The poor' is singular in Hebrew and stands for every poor person, so Literal uses the gender setting for 'him'. Balanced and Readable say what taking a levy meant for the poor. Readable puts the cause first and leaves out 'therefore'.

decisions.choice: "al pobre ... le" (L), with no gender span
decisions.reason: Spanish "el pobre" in the generic singular already includes women, so the English gender span (them / him) has no Spanish counterpart.

decisions.choice: "le pauvre ... de lui" with no gender setting
decisions.reason: French generic "le pauvre" and the "lui" that refers back to it already mean anyone poor, so French needs no setting where the English has one for the pronoun.

source.text: כִּ֤י יָדַ֨עְתִּי֙ רַבִּ֣ים פִּשְׁעֵיכֶ֔ם וַעֲצֻמִ֖ים חַטֹּֽאתֵיכֶ֑ם צֹרְרֵ֤י צַדִּיק֙ לֹ֣קְחֵי כֹ֔פֶר וְאֶבְיוֹנִ֖ים בַּשַּׁ֥עַר הִטּֽוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: For I know [that] many [are] your transgressions and numerous your sins, oppressors of [the] righteous, takers of a ransom; and [the] needy in the gate they turn aside.

en.L: For I know how many your transgressions are, \q and how numerous your sins, \q you who harass the righteous, who take a ransom, \q and turn aside the needy in the gate.
en.B: For I know how many your crimes are \q and how great your sins: \q you oppress the innocent and take bribes, \q and you push aside the poor in court.
en.R: I know how many times you have sinned \q and how great your sins are. \q You treat innocent people cruelly, and you take bribes. \q You keep poor people from getting justice in court.

es.L: Porque yo sé cuántas son {{plural_you:sus transgresiones|vuestras transgresiones}}, \q y cuán numerosos {{plural_you:sus pecados|vuestros pecados}}: \q {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, que {{plural_you:hostigan|hostigáis}} al justo, que {{plural_you:aceptan|aceptáis}} rescate, \q y {{plural_you:apartan|apartáis}} al necesitado en la puerta.
es.B: Porque yo sé cuántos son {{plural_you:sus delitos|vuestros delitos}} \q y cuán grandes {{plural_you:sus pecados|vuestros pecados}}: \q {{plural_you:oprimen|oprimís}} al inocente y {{plural_you:aceptan|aceptáis}} sobornos, \q y {{plural_you:atropellan|atropelláis}} al pobre en el tribunal.
es.R: Yo sé cuántas veces {{plural_you:han pecado|habéis pecado}} \q y cuán grandes son {{plural_you:sus pecados|vuestros pecados}}. \q {{plural_you:Tratan|Tratáis}} con crueldad a los inocentes y {{plural_you:aceptan|aceptáis}} sobornos. \q No {{plural_you:dejan|dejáis}} que los pobres reciban justicia en el tribunal.

fr.L: Car je sais combien nombreuses [sont] vos transgressions, \q et combien grands vos péchés, \q vous qui opprimez le juste, qui prenez une rançon, \q et qui écartez les indigents à la porte.
fr.B: Car je sais combien vos crimes sont nombreux \q et vos péchés énormes : \q vous opprimez l’innocent et vous acceptez des pots-de-vin, \q et vous écartez les pauvres au tribunal.
fr.R: Je sais combien de fois vous avez péché \q et combien vos péchés sont graves. \q Vous maltraitez les innocents et vous acceptez des pots-de-vin. \q Vous empêchez les pauvres d’obtenir justice au tribunal.

sw.L: Kwa maana najua jinsi maasi yenu yalivyo mengi, \q na jinsi dhambi zenu zilivyo nyingi, \q ninyi mnaomtesa mwenye haki, mnaopokea fidia, \q na kumgeuzia mbali mhitaji langoni.
sw.B: Kwa maana najua jinsi makosa yenu yalivyo mengi \q na jinsi dhambi zenu zilivyo kubwa: \q mnamdhulumu asiye na hatia na kupokea rushwa, \q na mnamsukuma kando maskini mahakamani.
sw.R: Najua ni mara ngapi mmetenda dhambi \q na jinsi dhambi zenu zilivyo kubwa. \q Mnawatendea ukatili watu wasio na hatia, na mnapokea rushwa. \q Mnawazuia maskini wasipate haki mahakamani.

decisions.choice: the righteous: the one in the right, the innocent party in a case
decisions.reason: In a court, the tsaddiq is the person who is in the right. These judges harass the innocent instead of clearing them.

decisions.choice: take a ransom: take a bribe to let the guilty go
decisions.reason: Kofer is money paid to buy someone free. The law forbids taking it to spare a murderer (Numbers 35:31); here judges take it to let the guilty go or to rule against the poor (1 Samuel 12:3).

decisions.choice: turn aside the needy in the gate: deny the poor a fair hearing in court
decisions.reason: To 'turn aside' a person, or their case, is to refuse them justice (Exodus 23:6; Isaiah 10:2; see 2:7).

decisions.choice: crimes (B), sinned (R); innocent; bribes (B, R)
decisions.reason: The terms note for Amos gives pesha' as 'transgression' at Literal, 'crime' or 'rebellion' at Balanced and 'sin' at Readable. Balanced and Readable say 'innocent' for the one in the right (m1) and 'bribes' for the ransom (m2).

source.text: לָכֵ֗ן הַמַּשְׂכִּ֛יל בָּעֵ֥ת הַהִ֖יא יִדֹּ֑ם כִּ֛י עֵ֥ת רָעָ֖ה הִֽיא׃

records.literal_gloss: Therefore the prudent at the time the that will be silent, for an evil time it [is].

en.L: Therefore the prudent will keep silent at that time, \q for it is an evil time.
en.B: So at such a time the prudent keep quiet, \q for it is an evil time.
en.R: That is why wise people keep quiet in times like these, \q because these are evil times.

es.L: Por tanto, el prudente callará en ese tiempo, \q porque es tiempo malo.
es.B: Por eso, en tiempos así el prudente se calla, \q porque es un tiempo malo.
es.R: Por eso los sabios se quedan callados en tiempos como estos, \q porque son tiempos malos.

fr.L: C’est pourquoi l’homme avisé se taira en ce temps-là, \q car c’est un temps mauvais.
fr.B: Aussi, en un tel temps, l’homme sensé se tait, \q car c’est un temps mauvais.
fr.R: C’est pourquoi les gens sages se taisent en des temps comme ceux-ci, \q parce que ce sont des temps mauvais.

sw.L: Kwa hiyo mwenye busara atanyamaza wakati huo, \q kwa maana ni wakati mbaya.
sw.B: Kwa hiyo wakati kama huo mwenye busara hunyamaza, \q kwa maana ni wakati mbaya.
sw.R: Ndiyo sababu watu wenye hekima hunyamaza nyakati kama hizi, \q kwa sababu ni nyakati mbaya.

decisions.choice: the prudent will keep silent: a sensible person keeps quiet, because speaking up is useless or dangerous
alternatives: the prudent will be destroyed at that time
the one who prospers will be struck dumb at that time
decisions.reason: The verse sounds like a proverb. It may describe the present: when the courts hate anyone who tells the truth (verse 10), a sensible person stays silent. Or it may look ahead to the evil time of judgment, when there will be nothing left to say. The verb can also mean to be destroyed, and the first word can mean one who prospers. Amos himself does not keep silent, so the line may be a bitter remark rather than advice.

decisions.choice: an evil time: a time of wickedness, and of the disaster it brings
decisions.reason: Ra'ah can mean moral evil or calamity, and both fit: the time is wicked, and disaster is coming because of it. Micah 2:3 uses the same phrase of a time of disaster.

source.text: דִּרְשׁוּ־ט֥וֹב וְאַל־רָ֖ע לְמַ֣עַן תִּֽחְי֑וּ וִיהִי־כֵ֞ן יְהוָ֧ה אֱלֹהֵֽי־צְבָא֛וֹת אִתְּכֶ֖ם כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר אֲמַרְתֶּֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Seek good and not evil, so that you may live, and so Yahweh God of hosts will be with you, just as you have said.

en.L: Seek good and not evil, so that you may live; \q and so {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God of hosts will be with you, just as you have said.
en.B: Seek good and not evil, so that you may live, \q and so that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God of Armies may truly be with you, as you claim {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is.
en.R: Seek what is good, not what is evil, so that you will live. \q Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God of Armies will really be with you, as you say {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is.

es.L: {{plural_you:Busquen|Buscad}} el bien y no el mal, para que {{plural_you:vivan|viváis}}; \q y así {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} Dios de los ejércitos estará con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, tal como {{plural_you:dicen|decís}}.
es.B: {{plural_you:Busquen|Buscad}} el bien y no el mal, para que {{plural_you:vivan|viváis}}, \q y para que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} Dios de los Ejércitos esté de verdad con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, como {{plural_you:ustedes afirman|vosotros afirmáis}} que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} está.
es.R: {{plural_you:Busquen|Buscad}} lo bueno y no lo malo, para que {{plural_you:vivan|viváis}}. \q Entonces {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} Dios de los Ejércitos estará de verdad con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, como {{plural_you:ustedes dicen|vosotros decís}} que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} está.

fr.L: Cherchez le bien et non le mal, afin que vous viviez ; \q et ainsi {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, Dieu des armées, sera avec vous, comme vous l’avez dit.
fr.B: Cherchez le bien et non le mal, afin de vivre, \q et afin que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, Dieu des armées, soit vraiment avec vous, comme vous le prétendez.
fr.R: Cherchez ce qui est bien, et non ce qui est mal, pour que vous viviez. \q Alors {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, Dieu des armées, sera vraiment avec vous, comme vous le dites.

sw.L: Tafuteni mema wala si mabaya, mpate kuishi; \q na hivyo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wa majeshi atakuwa pamoja nanyi, kama mlivyosema.
sw.B: Tafuteni mema wala si mabaya, mpate kuishi, \q ili {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wa majeshi awe pamoja nanyi kweli, kama mnavyodai.
sw.R: Tafuteni yaliyo mema, wala si yaliyo mabaya, ili mpate kuishi. \q Ndipo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wa majeshi atakuwa pamoja nanyi kweli, kama mnavyosema.

decisions.choice: seek good: doing good is the way of seeking the LORD
decisions.reason: Verses 4 and 6 say 'Seek me' and 'Seek the LORD'; here it is 'Seek good'. Seeking God and doing what is right are one thing, not two.

decisions.choice: just as you have said: the people claim that God is with them
decisions.reason: The people said that the LORD God of hosts was with them, perhaps in their worship or their battle cries, and felt secure (compare Micah 3:11). Amos turns the slogan into a condition: he will be with them if they seek good.

decisions.choice: the LORD God of hosts (L); the LORD God of Armies (B, R)
decisions.reason: YHWH 'elohe tseva'ot is the title 'the LORD of hosts' with 'God' added. It keeps the wording settled for 'the God of hosts' (Hosea 12:6): 'hosts' at Literal, 'Armies' at Balanced and Readable. The hosts are the armies of heaven and earth that the LORD commands.

decisions.choice: as you claim he is (B); as you say he is (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the people 'have said', that the LORD is with them (m2).

decisions.choice: "kama mnavyodai" (B); "kama mnavyosema" (R), with no span
decisions.reason: The English adds "he is" with a deity_pronoun span; Swahili says the same with the verb alone, so there is no free pronoun to carry the span.

source.text: שִׂנְאוּ־רָע֙ וְאֶ֣הֱבוּ ט֔וֹב וְהַצִּ֥יגוּ בַשַּׁ֖עַר מִשְׁפָּ֑ט אוּלַ֗י יֶֽחֱנַ֛ן יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵֽי־צְבָא֖וֹת שְׁאֵרִ֥ית יוֹסֵֽף׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Hate evil and love good, and set up in the gate justice; perhaps Yahweh God of hosts will be gracious [to the] remnant of Joseph.

en.L: Hate evil and love good, \q and establish justice in the gate; \q perhaps {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God of hosts will be gracious to the remnant of Joseph.
en.B: Hate evil and love good; \q establish justice in the courts. \q It may be that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God of Armies will be gracious to the remnant of Joseph.
en.R: Hate what is evil and love what is good. \q Make sure that the courts are fair. \q Then perhaps {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God of Armies will be kind to the people of Israel who are left.

es.L: {{plural_you:Aborrezcan|Aborreced}} el mal y {{plural_you:amen|amad}} el bien, \q y {{plural_you:establezcan|estableced}} el derecho en la puerta; \q quizá {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} Dios de los ejércitos tenga piedad del remanente de José.
es.B: {{plural_you:Odien|Odiad}} el mal y {{plural_you:amen|amad}} el bien; \q {{plural_you:establezcan|estableced}} el derecho en los tribunales. \q Puede ser que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} Dios de los Ejércitos tenga piedad del remanente de José.
es.R: {{plural_you:Odien|Odiad}} lo malo y {{plural_you:amen|amad}} lo bueno. \q {{plural_you:Asegúrense|Aseguraos}} de que en los tribunales se haga justicia. \q Entonces tal vez {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} Dios de los Ejércitos sea bondadoso con los israelitas que queden.

fr.L: Haïssez le mal et aimez le bien, \q et établissez le droit à la porte ; \q peut-être {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, Dieu des armées, fera-t-il grâce au reste de Joseph.
fr.B: Haïssez le mal et aimez le bien ; \q faites régner le droit au tribunal. \q Il se peut que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, Dieu des armées, fasse grâce au reste de Joseph.
fr.R: Détestez ce qui est mal et aimez ce qui est bien. \q Veillez à ce que les tribunaux soient justes. \q Alors peut-être {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, Dieu des armées, sera bon pour ceux qui restent du peuple d’Israël.

sw.L: Chukieni mabaya na kupenda mema, \q mkaithibitishe hukumu langoni; \q huenda {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wa majeshi atawafadhili mabaki ya Yusufu.
sw.B: Chukieni mabaya na kupenda mema; \q simamisheni haki mahakamani. \q Huenda {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wa majeshi atawafadhili mabaki ya Yusufu.
sw.R: Chukieni yaliyo mabaya na kupenda yaliyo mema. \q Hakikisheni kwamba mahakama zinatenda haki. \q Ndipo huenda {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wa majeshi atawahurumia watu wa Israeli waliobaki.

decisions.choice: perhaps: there is hope, but no promise
decisions.reason: Even if the people turn, the LORD is not bound to spare them; his mercy cannot be taken for granted (Joel 2:14; Jonah 3:9; Zephaniah 2:3). The offer is real, but it is not a bargain.

decisions.choice: the remnant of Joseph: those who will be left after the judgment
decisions.reason: Amos has already said that only a tenth will survive (verse 3). The remnant is what remains of the northern kingdom, Joseph's house (verse 6). Even the hope he holds out is for survivors.

decisions.choice: in the courts (B); make sure that the courts are fair; the people of Israel who are left (R)
decisions.reason: 'In the gate' means in court (verse 10). Readable says 'the people of Israel who are left' for 'the remnant of Joseph' (5:6).

decisions.choice: "el remanente de José" (L, B); "los israelitas que queden" (R)
decisions.reason: Remnant as the terms note sets (R "los que queden").

source.text: לָ֠כֵן כֹּֽה־אָמַ֨ר יְהוָ֜ה אֱלֹהֵ֤י צְבָאוֹת֙ אֲדֹנָ֔י בְּכָל־רְחֹב֣וֹת מִסְפֵּ֔ד וּבְכָל־חוּצ֖וֹת יֹאמְר֣וּ הוֹ־ה֑וֹ וְקָרְא֤וּ אִכָּר֙ אֶל־אֵ֔בֶל וּמִסְפֵּ֖ד אֶל־י֥וֹדְעֵי נֶֽהִי׃

records.literal_gloss: Therefore thus says Yahweh God of hosts, [the] Lord: in all squares [there will be] wailing, and in all streets they will say, Alas! Alas! And they will call [the] farmer to mourning, and wailing to those who know lamentation.

en.L: Therefore thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God of hosts, the Lord: \q In all the squares [there will be] wailing, \q and in all the streets they will say, "Alas! Alas!" \q They will call the farmer to mourning, \q and [call] to wailing those skilled in lament.
en.B: Therefore {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God of Armies, the Lord, says this: \q There will be wailing in every square, \q and in every street people will cry, "Alas! Alas!" \q They will call the farmers to mourn \q and the professional mourners to wail.
en.R: So this is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God of Armies, the Lord, says: \q People will be crying in all the town squares. \q In every street they will cry out, "How sad! How sad!" \q They will call farmers in from the fields to weep. \q They will call for those who are paid to mourn for the dead.

es.L: Por tanto, así dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} Dios de los ejércitos, el Señor: \q En todas las plazas [habrá] llanto, \q y en todas las calles dirán: «¡Ay! ¡Ay!». \q Llamarán al labrador al duelo, \q y [llamarán] al llanto a los expertos en lamentaciones.
es.B: Por eso, {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} Dios de los Ejércitos, el Señor, dice esto: \q En todas las plazas habrá llanto, \q y en todas las calles la gente gritará: «¡Ay! ¡Ay!». \q Llamarán a los labradores a hacer duelo \q y a las plañideras a llorar.
es.R: Por eso, esto es lo que dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} Dios de los Ejércitos, el Señor: \q La gente llorará en todas las plazas de la ciudad. \q En todas las calles gritarán: «¡Ay! ¡Ay!». \q Llamarán a los campesinos que están en el campo para que vengan a llorar. \q Llamarán a los que cobran por llorar a los muertos.

fr.L: C’est pourquoi ainsi parle {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, Dieu des armées, le Seigneur : \q Sur toutes les places, [il y aura] des lamentations, \q et dans toutes les rues on dira : « Hélas ! Hélas ! » \q On appellera le laboureur au deuil, \q et aux lamentations ceux qui savent la complainte.
fr.B: C’est pourquoi {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, Dieu des armées, le Seigneur, dit ceci : \q Sur toutes les places, on se lamentera, \q et dans toutes les rues on criera : « Hélas ! Hélas ! » \q On appellera les laboureurs à prendre le deuil \q et les pleureuses de métier à se lamenter.
fr.R: Alors voici ce que dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, Dieu des armées, le Seigneur : \q Sur toutes les places des villes, les gens pleureront. \q Dans toutes les rues, ils crieront : « Quelle tristesse ! Quelle tristesse ! » \q On fera venir les paysans des champs pour pleurer. \q On appellera ceux qu’on paie pour pleurer les morts.

sw.L: Kwa hiyo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wa majeshi, Bwana, asema hivi: \q Katika viwanja vyote [kutakuwa na] maombolezo, \q na katika njia zote watasema, "Ole! Ole!" \q Watamwita mkulima aje kuomboleza, \q na [kuwaita] kwenye maombolezo wale wajuzi wa kulia.
sw.B: Kwa hiyo hivi ndivyo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wa majeshi, Bwana, asemavyo: \q Kutakuwa na maombolezo katika kila uwanja, \q na katika kila njia watu watalia, "Ole! Ole!" \q Watawaita wakulima waje kuomboleza \q na waombolezaji wa kulipwa waje kulia.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo hili ndilo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wa majeshi, Bwana, analosema: \q Watu watakuwa wakilia katika viwanja vyote vya mji. \q Katika kila njia watapiga kelele, "Inasikitisha! Inasikitisha!" \q Watawaita wakulima kutoka mashambani waje kulia. \q Watawaita wale wanaolipwa kuwaombolezea wafu.

decisions.choice: those who know lamentation: professional mourners
decisions.reason: At a funeral, women skilled in lament were called in to lead the weeping (Jeremiah 9:16-17; 2 Chronicles 35:25). There will be so many dead that even farmers are called from the fields to mourn, and the professional mourners will be needed everywhere.

decisions.choice: Alas! Alas!: the cry of mourning for the dead
decisions.reason: Ho is the cry of grief at a funeral (1 Kings 13:30; Jeremiah 22:18), related to hoy, 'woe' (5:18).

decisions.choice: the Lord: a further title after 'the LORD God of hosts'
decisions.reason: The title is unusual: Adonai, 'the Lord', stands at the end, after 'the LORD God of hosts'. It stresses that the one who speaks is master over all.

decisions.choice: How sad! How sad! (R); in from the fields (R)
decisions.reason: The funeral cry is 'Alas' at Literal and Balanced and 'How sad' at Readable, as Jeremiah 22:18. Readable adds 'in from the fields' to show why farmers are named.

decisions.choice: "¡Ay! ¡Ay!" at every level
decisions.reason: The funeral cry ho ho is "¡Ay! ¡Ay!" at every level, as the terms note sets, where the English R has "How sad!"; it is the natural Spanish cry of mourning.

decisions.choice: "las plañideras" (B)
decisions.reason: Those skilled in lament are the professional mourners, as Jeremiah 9:16 in Spanish.

decisions.choice: "Hélas ! Hélas !" (L, B); "Quelle tristesse ! Quelle tristesse !" (R)
decisions.reason: The funeral cry follows the French Jeremiah 22:18, as the term sheet sets.

decisions.choice: "Ole! Ole!" (L, B); "Inasikitisha! Inasikitisha!" (R)
decisions.reason: The funeral cry ho ho, as the term sheet sets for the cry of mourning.

source.text: וּבְכָל־כְּרָמִ֖ים מִסְפֵּ֑ד כִּֽי־אֶעֱבֹ֥ר בְּקִרְבְּךָ֖ אָמַ֥ר יְהוָֽה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And in all vineyards [there will be] wailing, for I will pass through your midst, says Yahweh.

en.L: And in all the vineyards [there will be] wailing, \q for I will pass through your midst, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: There will be wailing in every vineyard, \q for I will pass through the middle of you, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: People will cry in all the vineyards, \q because I will come through your land to punish you, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

es.L: Y en todas las viñas [habrá] llanto, \q porque pasaré por en medio de ti, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.
es.B: Habrá llanto en todas las viñas, \q porque pasaré por en medio de ti, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.
es.R: La gente llorará en todas las viñas, \q porque pasaré por tu tierra para castigarte, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.

fr.L: Et dans toutes les vignes, [il y aura] des lamentations, \q car je passerai au milieu de toi, dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.
fr.B: Dans toutes les vignes on se lamentera, \q car je passerai au milieu de toi, dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.
fr.R: Les gens pleureront dans toutes les vignes, \q parce que je traverserai ton pays pour te punir, dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.

sw.L: Na katika mashamba yote ya mizabibu [kutakuwa na] maombolezo, \q kwa maana nitapita katikati yako, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.B: Kutakuwa na maombolezo katika kila shamba la mizabibu, \q kwa maana nitapita katikati yenu, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.R: Watu watalia katika mashamba yote ya mizabibu, \q kwa sababu nitapita katika nchi yenu ili kuwaadhibu, anasema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.

decisions.choice: I will pass through your midst: as the LORD passed through Egypt on the night of the Passover
decisions.reason: In Exodus 12:12 the LORD says 'I will pass through the land of Egypt' to strike the firstborn. Now he will pass through Israel in judgment, as if Israel had become Egypt. Compare 7:8 and 8:2, where he says he will no longer 'pass by' them, that is, spare them.

decisions.choice: wailing in the vineyards: even the places of joy will be places of mourning
decisions.reason: The grape harvest was a time of singing and shouting (Isaiah 16:10; Judges 9:27). Now there will be wailing there too.

decisions.choice: come through your land to punish you (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says why the LORD will pass through (m1).

decisions.choice: tú in "en medio de ti"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "your" is singular here, Israel as one person, so Spanish uses tú.

source.text: ה֥וֹי הַמִּתְאַוִּ֖ים אֶת־י֣וֹם יְהוָ֑ה לָמָּה־זֶּ֥ה לָכֶ֛ם י֥וֹם יְהוָ֖ה הוּא־חֹ֥שֶׁךְ וְלֹא־אֽוֹר׃

records.literal_gloss: Woe [to] those who desire the day of Yahweh! Why [is] this to you, the day of Yahweh? It [is] darkness and not light.

en.L: Woe, you who long for the day of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}! \q What [good is] the day of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} to you? It [is] darkness, and not light.
en.B: Woe to you who long for the day of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}! \q Why do you want the day of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}? It will be darkness, not light.
en.R: How terrible it will be for you who want the day of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} to come! \q Why do you want that day? It will be a day of darkness, not light.

es.L: ¡Ay de los que anhelan el día {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}! \q ¿De qué {{plural_you:les|os}} [servirá] el día {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}? Tinieblas [será], y no luz.
es.B: ¡Ay de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, los que {{plural_you:anhelan|anheláis}} el día {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}! \q ¿Para qué {{plural_you:quieren|queréis}} el día {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}? Será tinieblas, no luz.
es.R: ¡Qué terrible será para {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, los que {{plural_you:quieren|queréis}} que llegue el día {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}! \q ¿Para qué {{plural_you:quieren|queréis}} ese día? Será un día de oscuridad, no de luz.

fr.L: Malheur, vous qui désirez le jour {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} ! \q Qu’[est] pour vous le jour {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} ? Il [est] ténèbres et non lumière.
fr.B: Malheur à vous qui désirez le jour {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} ! \q Pourquoi voulez-vous le jour {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} ? Ce sera les ténèbres et non la lumière.
fr.R: Quel malheur pour vous qui voulez que le jour {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} arrive ! \q Pourquoi voulez-vous ce jour-là ? Ce sera un jour de ténèbres, et non de lumière.

sw.L: Ole, ninyi mnaoitamani siku ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}! \q Siku ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} [ni nini] kwenu? Ni giza, wala si nuru.
sw.B: Ole wenu mnaoitamani siku ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}! \q Kwa nini mnaitaka siku ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}? Itakuwa giza, wala si nuru.
sw.R: Itakuwa vibaya sana kwenu ninyi mnaotamani siku ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ije! \q Kwa nini mnaitaka siku hiyo? Itakuwa siku ya giza, wala si ya nuru.

decisions.choice: the day of the LORD: the day when the LORD acts in power, which Israel expected to bring victory and Amos says will bring judgment on Israel
decisions.reason: This is the earliest use of 'the day of the LORD' among the prophets; the main note is at Joel 1:15. Amos's hearers knew the phrase and looked forward to that day as the time when the LORD would rise up to defeat their enemies and bless his people. Amos turns their hope upside down: the day will be darkness for Israel itself, because Israel too is among the guilty. Later prophets take up the same warning (Isaiah 13:6, 9; Zephaniah 1:14-18; Joel 2:1-2).

decisions.choice: woe: the cry of mourning over people as good as dead
decisions.reason: Hoy is the cry raised at a funeral (compare 5:16). Spoken over the living, it announces their death. Isaiah's 'woe' sayings use it the same way (Isaiah 5:8).

decisions.choice: darkness, not light: disaster, not deliverance
decisions.reason: Light stands for safety, blessing and salvation, darkness for disaster and judgment (Isaiah 9:1; 13:10).

decisions.choice: Woe, you who (L); Woe to you who (B); How terrible it will be for you who (R); the day of the LORD at every level
decisions.reason: Hoy follows Isaiah's wording at each level, and 'the day of the LORD' keeps the same words at every level, as Isaiah 13:6. The Hebrew says 'those who long for' and then turns to 'you'; the English uses 'you' throughout.

decisions.choice: "¡Ay de ...!" (L, B); "¡Qué terrible será para ...!" (R)
decisions.reason: Hoy as the Spanish of Isaiah has it; L keeps the Hebrew third person, B and R speak to the hearers, as the English B and R do.

decisions.choice: "Malheur, vous qui" (L); "Malheur à vous qui" (B); "Quel malheur pour vous qui" (R)
decisions.reason: The French prophets' wording for hoy at each level.

decisions.choice: "Ole, ..." (L); "Ole wenu ..." (B); "Itakuwa vibaya sana kwenu ..." (R)
decisions.reason: Hoy, as in Isaiah; Balanced has "wenu" because the woe is addressed to them. Amos turns the hoped-for day of the LORD against Israel itself.

source.text: כַּאֲשֶׁ֨ר יָנ֥וּס אִישׁ֙ מִפְּנֵ֣י הָאֲרִ֔י וּפְגָע֖וֹ הַדֹּ֑ב וּבָ֣א הַבַּ֔יִת וְסָמַ֤ךְ יָדוֹ֙ עַל־הַקִּ֔יר וּנְשָׁכ֖וֹ הַנָּחָֽשׁ׃

records.literal_gloss: As when a man flees from before the lion, and the bear meets him; and he goes [into] the house and leans his hand on the wall, and the snake bites him.

en.L: As if a man fled from the lion, \q and the bear met him; \q and he went into the house \q and leaned his hand against the wall, \q and the snake bit him.
en.B: It will be as when a man runs from a lion \q and a bear meets him, \q or he goes home \q and leans his hand against the wall, \q and a snake bites him.
en.R: It will be like a man who runs away from a lion, \q only to meet a bear. \q Or he gets home safely \q and leans his hand against the wall, \q and a snake bites him.

es.L: Como si un hombre huyera delante del león, \q y le saliera al encuentro el oso; \q y entrara en la casa \q y apoyara su mano en la pared, \q y lo mordiera la serpiente.
es.B: Será como cuando un hombre huye de un león \q y se topa con un oso, \q o entra en su casa \q y apoya la mano en la pared, \q y lo muerde una serpiente.
es.R: Será como un hombre que huye de un león \q y se encuentra con un oso. \q O llega a salvo a su casa \q y apoya la mano en la pared, \q y una serpiente lo muerde.

fr.L: Comme si un homme fuyait devant le lion, \q et que l’ours le rencontrait ; \q et qu’il entrait dans la maison \q et appuyait sa main contre le mur, \q et que le serpent le mordait.
fr.B: Ce sera comme quand un homme fuit devant un lion \q et tombe sur un ours, \q ou qu’il rentre chez lui, \q s’appuie de la main contre le mur, \q et qu’un serpent le mord.
fr.R: Ce sera comme un homme qui s’enfuit devant un lion, \q et qui tombe sur un ours. \q Ou bien il arrive chez lui sain et sauf, \q il appuie la main contre le mur, \q et un serpent le mord.

sw.L: Kama mtu aliyemkimbia simba, \q naye dubu akakutana naye; \q naye akaingia nyumbani \q akauegemeza mkono wake ukutani, \q naye nyoka akamwuma.
sw.B: Itakuwa kama mtu anayemkimbia simba \q naye dubu akakutana naye, \q au anaingia nyumbani \q na kuuegemeza mkono wake ukutani, \q naye nyoka akamwuma.
sw.R: Itakuwa kama mtu anayemkimbia simba, \q kumbe anakutana na dubu. \q Au anafika nyumbani salama \q na kuuegemeza mkono wake ukutani, \q naye nyoka akamwuma.

decisions.choice: a picture of the day of the LORD: no way of escape
decisions.reason: The man escapes one danger only to meet another, and when he reaches the safety of his own house, he is bitten there. So it will be on the day of the LORD: Israel will not escape, wherever it turns. Amos has used the picture of the lion before (3:4, 8, 12), and 9:1-4 says the same without a picture.

decisions.choice: only to; gets home safely (R)
decisions.reason: Readable adds 'only to' and 'safely' to bring out the point of the picture: each time the man thinks he has escaped (m1).

source.text: הֲלֹא־חֹ֛שֶׁךְ י֥וֹם יְהוָ֖ה וְלֹא־א֑וֹר וְאָפֵ֖ל וְלֹא־נֹ֥גַֽהּ לֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: [Is] not darkness the day of Yahweh, and not light, and gloom and no brightness to it?

en.L: Is not the day of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} darkness, and not light, \q and gloom with no brightness in it?
en.B: Will not the day of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} be darkness, not light, \q pitch dark, with no brightness in it?
en.R: Yes, the day of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will be darkness, not light. \q It will be completely dark, with no light at all.

es.L: ¿No [será] el día {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} tinieblas, y no luz, \q oscuridad, sin resplandor alguno?
es.B: ¿No será el día {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} tinieblas y no luz, \q oscuridad total, sin ningún resplandor?
es.R: Sí, el día {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} será oscuridad, no luz. \q Será completamente oscuro, sin nada de luz.

fr.L: Le jour {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} n’[est]-il pas ténèbres, et non lumière, \q obscurité sans éclat ?
fr.B: Le jour {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} ne sera-t-il pas ténèbres et non lumière, \q nuit noire, sans aucune clarté ?
fr.R: Oui, le jour {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} sera ténèbres, et non lumière. \q Il fera complètement noir, sans aucune lumière.

sw.L: Je, siku ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} si giza, wala si nuru, \q na utusitusi usio na mwangaza ndani yake?
sw.B: Je, siku ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} haitakuwa giza, wala si nuru, \q giza totoro lisilo na mwangaza wowote?
sw.R: Naam, siku ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} itakuwa giza, wala si nuru. \q Itakuwa giza kabisa, bila mwanga wowote.

decisions.choice: Is not ...?: a question that expects the answer 'Yes, it is'
decisions.reason: The question repeats the end of verse 18 and drives it home. The answer is not in doubt.

decisions.choice: gloom ... no brightness: thick darkness without a glimmer
decisions.reason: 'Afel is the deep dark of night (Isaiah 59:9). Nogah is brightness or the first glow of light; not even that will be left.

decisions.choice: a statement, not a question (R)
decisions.reason: Readable gives the answer the question expects (m1) as a plain statement.

source.text: שָׂנֵ֥אתִי מָאַ֖סְתִּי חַגֵּיכֶ֑ם וְלֹ֥א אָרִ֖יחַ בְּעַצְּרֹֽתֵיכֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: I hate, I reject your feasts, and I do not delight in your assemblies.

en.L: I hate, I reject your feasts, \q and I take no delight in your solemn assemblies.
en.B: I hate, I despise your festivals; \q I take no pleasure in your sacred assemblies.
en.R: I hate your religious festivals. I cannot stand them. \q I am not pleased with your special meetings for worship.

es.L: Aborrezco, desprecio {{plural_you:sus fiestas|vuestras fiestas}}, \q y no me complazco en {{plural_you:sus asambleas solemnes|vuestras asambleas solemnes}}.
es.B: Odio, desprecio {{plural_you:sus festivales|vuestros festivales}}; \q no me agradan {{plural_you:sus asambleas sagradas|vuestras asambleas sagradas}}.
es.R: Odio {{plural_you:sus fiestas religiosas|vuestras fiestas religiosas}}. No las soporto. \q No me agradan {{plural_you:sus reuniones especiales|vuestras reuniones especiales}} de adoración.

fr.L: Je hais, je rejette vos fêtes, \q et je ne prends pas plaisir à vos assemblées solennelles.
fr.B: Je hais, je méprise vos fêtes ; \q vos assemblées sacrées ne me plaisent pas.
fr.R: Je déteste vos fêtes religieuses. Je ne peux pas les supporter. \q Vos réunions spéciales pour le culte ne me plaisent pas.

sw.L: Nazichukia, nazikataa sikukuu zenu, \q wala sifurahii makusanyiko yenu matakatifu.
sw.B: Nazichukia, nazidharau sikukuu zenu; \q sipendezwi na mikutano yenu mitakatifu.
sw.R: Nazichukia sikukuu zenu za kidini. Siwezi kuzivumilia. \q Sipendezwi na mikutano yenu maalum ya ibada.

decisions.choice: the LORD rejects worship offered by those who do injustice
decisions.reason: Amos is not rejecting worship as such; verses 21-24 set worship against justice. The same is said in Isaiah 1:11-17, Hosea 6:6 and Micah 6:6-8: sacrifices offered by people who oppress the poor are hateful to God.

decisions.choice: feasts and assemblies: the pilgrimage festivals and the gatherings for worship
decisions.reason: Chag is a pilgrimage feast, such as Passover, Weeks and Booths, when the people went to the shrines (Exodus 23:14-17). 'Atsarah is a holy gathering on a feast day (Leviticus 23:36; Isaiah 1:13).

decisions.choice: I take no delight: literally 'I will not smell'
decisions.reason: The verb means to smell, and is used of the LORD accepting the smell of an offering (Genesis 8:21). Leviticus 26:31 warns, 'I will not smell your pleasing aromas.' He refuses the scent of their sacrifices.

decisions.choice: religious festivals; special meetings for worship (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says what kind of feasts and assemblies are meant (m2).

source.text: כִּ֣י אִם־תַּעֲלוּ־לִ֥י עֹל֛וֹת וּמִנְחֹתֵיכֶ֖ם לֹ֣א אֶרְצֶ֑ה וְשֶׁ֥לֶם מְרִיאֵיכֶ֖ם לֹ֥א אַבִּֽיט׃

records.literal_gloss: For if you offer up to me burnt offerings and your grain offerings, I will not accept [them]; and the peace offering of your fatlings I will not look at.

en.L: Even if you offer up to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} burnt offerings and your grain offerings, I will not accept [them]; \q and the peace offerings of your fattened animals I will not look at.
en.B: Even if you sacrifice burnt offerings and grain offerings to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, I will not accept them; \q I will not look at the peace offerings of your fattened animals.
en.R: Even if you bring {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} burnt offerings and grain offerings, I will not accept them. \q I will not even look at the fat animals you bring as peace offerings.

es.L: Aunque {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} {{plural_you:ofrezcan|ofrezcáis}} holocaustos y {{plural_you:sus ofrendas de cereal|vuestras ofrendas de cereal}}, no [las] aceptaré; \q ni miraré los sacrificios de paz de {{plural_you:sus animales engordados|vuestros animales engordados}}.
es.B: Aunque {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} {{plural_you:ofrezcan|ofrezcáis}} holocaustos y ofrendas de cereal, no los aceptaré; \q no miraré los sacrificios de paz de {{plural_you:sus animales engordados|vuestros animales engordados}}.
es.R: Aunque {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} {{plural_you:traigan|traigáis}} holocaustos y ofrendas de cereal, no los aceptaré. \q Ni siquiera miraré los animales gordos que {{plural_you:traen|traéis}} como sacrificios de paz.

fr.L: Même si vous {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}offrez des holocaustes et vos offrandes de grain, je ne [les] accepterai pas ; \q et les sacrifices de paix de vos bêtes grasses, je ne [les] regarderai pas.
fr.B: Même si vous {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}offrez des holocaustes et des offrandes de grain, je ne les accepterai pas ; \q je ne regarderai pas les sacrifices de paix de vos bêtes engraissées.
fr.R: Même si vous {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}apportez des holocaustes et des offrandes de grain, je ne les accepterai pas. \q Je ne regarderai même pas les bêtes grasses que vous apportez comme sacrifices de paix.

sw.L: Hata mkinitolea sadaka za kuteketezwa na sadaka zenu za nafaka, sitazikubali; \q na sadaka za amani za wanyama wenu walionona sitaziangalia.
sw.B: Hata mkinitolea sadaka za kuteketezwa na sadaka za nafaka, sitazikubali; \q sitaziangalia sadaka za amani za wanyama wenu walionona.
sw.R: Hata mkiniletea sadaka za kuteketezwa na sadaka za nafaka, sitazikubali. \q Sitawaangalia hata wanyama wanono mnaoleta kama sadaka za amani.

decisions.choice: burnt offerings, grain offerings, peace offerings: the main kinds of sacrifice
decisions.reason: A burnt offering was burned whole on the altar (Leviticus 1). A grain offering was flour or grain with oil (Leviticus 2). The peace offering was shared: part was burned, and the worshipers ate the rest in a meal (Leviticus 3; 7:11-15). The LORD rejects all three.

decisions.choice: accept ... look at: receive with favor
decisions.reason: Ratsah is the word for the LORD accepting an offering and the one who brings it (Leviticus 1:4). To 'look at' an offering is to regard it with favor, as the LORD looked at Abel's offering (Genesis 4:4). He will do neither.

decisions.choice: "holocaustos", "ofrendas de cereal", "sacrificios de paz"
decisions.reason: The three sacrifices in the words of the Spanish Pentateuch (Leviticus 10:14).

decisions.choice: no deity_pronoun span in "mkinitolea"
decisions.reason: God is the object marker "-ni-" inside the verb, which cannot take a capital; the same holds for "Me" in verses 23 and 25.

source.text: הָסֵ֥ר מֵעָלַ֖י הֲמ֣וֹן שִׁרֶ֑יךָ וְזִמְרַ֥ת נְבָלֶ֖יךָ לֹ֥א אֶשְׁמָֽע׃

records.literal_gloss: Remove from me the noise of your songs, and the music of your harps I will not listen to.

en.L: Take away from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} the noise of your songs; \q the music of your harps I will not listen to.
en.B: Take the noise of your songs away from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}; \q I will not listen to the music of your harps.
en.R: Take your noisy songs away from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}! \q I will not listen to the music of your harps.

es.L: Quita de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} el ruido de tus cantos; \q no escucharé la música de tus arpas.
es.B: Aparta de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} el ruido de tus canciones; \q no escucharé la música de tus arpas.
es.R: ¡Llévate de mi presencia tus canciones ruidosas! \q No escucharé la música de tus arpas.

fr.L: Éloigne de {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} le bruit de tes chants ; \q la musique de tes harpes, je ne l’écouterai pas.
fr.B: Éloigne de {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} le vacarme de tes chants ; \q je n’écouterai pas la musique de tes harpes.
fr.R: Arrête tes chants bruyants devant {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} ! \q Je n’écouterai pas la musique de tes harpes.

sw.L: Niondoleeni kelele za nyimbo zenu; \q sauti ya vinubi vyenu sitaisikiliza.
sw.B: Niondoleeni kelele za nyimbo zenu; \q sitasikiliza muziki wa vinubi vyenu.
sw.R: Niondoleeni nyimbo zenu zenye kelele! \q Sitasikiliza muziki wa vinubi vyenu.

decisions.choice: noise: the loud din of a crowd
decisions.reason: Hamon is the roar of a crowd or of many voices. The temple songs that the singers think beautiful are only noise to the LORD.

decisions.choice: remove ... your songs ... your harps: spoken to the people as one
decisions.reason: The command and the word 'your' in this verse are singular, though verses 21-22 address the people as 'you' plural. The LORD speaks to Israel as one worshiper, or to each one in it.

decisions.choice: tú in this verse
decisions.reason: The Hebrew turns to the singular here, the people spoken to as one, so Spanish uses tú, as the meaning decision notes.

decisions.choice: "Éloigne", "tes": the singular
decisions.reason: The Hebrew speaks to the people as one here (the meaning decision), and French follows its number.

source.text: וְיִגַּ֥ל כַּמַּ֖יִם מִשְׁפָּ֑ט וּצְדָקָ֖ה כְּנַ֥חַל אֵיתָֽן׃

records.literal_gloss: But let roll like the waters justice, and righteousness like a stream ever-flowing.

en.L: But let justice roll on like the waters, \q and righteousness like an ever-flowing stream.
en.B: Instead, let justice roll on like water, \q and righteousness like a stream that never runs dry.
